records.name: Nicolae Cican
events: returned to Romania by 1913/1914; documented in a 1914 Romanian diplomatic memorandum as Nicolae Cican, merchant and former American resident
enlisted in the Romanian Army and died during World War I
died 19 February 1918 in Chișinău, Bessarabia; contemporary newspaper identifies him as sub-lieutenant Nicolae Cican, Romanian from Macedonia
records.notes: Identified by the Aromanian Cultural Society Farsharotu as a founder; independent scholarly material also describes Nicolae Cican as an early immigrant to America and founder of the society. No relationship to other Cican records is inferred. A scholarly Balamaci source reports that Nicolae Cican had spent 12–13 years in America, returned to Romania, lost his home and funds in 1914, later enlisted in the Romanian Army and died during World War I. Exact enlistment unit, death date and place require primary military/casualty records. A contemporary 1914 newspaper independently places him in Corcea during the March 1914 violence and reports the burning of his house and his survival. This corroborates the later scholarly account of his 1914 return and circumstances. A contemporary 20 February 1918 issue of România Nouă reports that sub-lieutenant Nicolae Cican, described as a Romanian from Macedonia, died suddenly in Chișinău on 19 February 1918 and announces his funeral. This strongly corroborates the previously secondary report that Nicolae Cican served in the Romanian Army and died during WWI. A 1915 published testimony identifies Spiru Cican explicitly as Nicolae Cican's brother and tenant in Nicolae's Corcea house. This is the first strong direct sibling evidence between the two existing records.

records.name: Spiru Cican
records.notes: Named by the Society as a founder. Relationship to other Cican people remains unestablished. A 1915 published testimony explicitly identifies Spiru Cican as Nicolae Cican's brother and tenant in Nicolae's Corcea house, independently strengthening the relationship between these two existing person records.

records.name: Nasta Cican
records.notes: Named by the Society as a founder. Relationship to other Cican people remains unestablished.

records.name: Dina Cican
records.notes: Named by the Society as a founder. Relationship to other Cican people remains unestablished. The 1915 publication also contains a contemporary testimony by Dina Cican concerning the Corcea property destruction. This connects her to the event, but does not establish her exact relationship to Nicolae or Spiru. The 1915 text styles this historical Dina Cican as 'D-l Dina Cican' (Mr. Dina Cican), so the archive preserves the source's male honorific rather than inferring a modern gender identity. The source still does not establish his relationship to Nicolae or Spiru.
